summary: the metal suite on i686 with its acceptance script taken from a private copy of metal_accept.sh, laid out beside the tree's su_command.sh

argv: rm -rf ${WORK}/accept && mkdir -p ${WORK}/accept/tests/system/accept && ln -s ${TREE}/build ${WORK}/accept/build && ln -s ${TREE}/krffs ${WORK}/accept/krffs && cp ${SRC}/tests/system/accept/metal_accept.sh tests/system/accept/su_command.sh ${WORK}/accept/tests/system/accept/

log=build/images/metal-test.metal.log; rm -f $log; status=0; METAL_ACCEPT_SCRIPT=${WORK}/accept/tests/system/accept/metal_accept.sh ARCH=i686 tests/run metal </dev/null || status=$?; [ ! -f $log ] || cat $log; exit $status

faults.name: busy-fat
faults.summary: the acceptance holds a file of the stick open while it unmounts it, so the unmount fails though the writes were flushed

lines: metal-test: the acceptance flushed the stick's writes

faults.name: short-mbr
faults.summary: the acceptance reads no bytes of the MBR, which dd reports as a success

lines: FAIL: disk: the published whole-disk window did not supply one complete sector
